_README: Curated operation documentation, keyed by `METHOD /path` exactly as the router declares it.
scripts/generate-openapi.mjs merges these into docs/openapi.yaml; anything missing still appears
with a summary derived from its path, so this file is where a description is made *better*, never
where the document is completed. Add an entry when an operation's purpose is not obvious from its
path, when it is what an integrator will reach for, or when its behaviour needs a warning.

POST /api/auth/login.summary: Sign in and receive a session token
POST /api/auth/login.description: Email and password in, a bearer token out. When MFA is enabled the answer is an mfaToken instead, which POST /api/auth/verify-mfa exchanges for the real token. A token is what the Authorization header carries for a person; a program should use an API key instead.

GET /api/auth/me.summary: The signed-in identity, with its permissions
GET /api/auth/me.description: The cheapest way for a client to confirm a credential works and to learn the permissions it holds.

POST /api/auth/mfa/verify.summary: Exchange an MFA challenge for a session token
POST /api/auth/mfa/verify.description: The second half of MFA sign-in: the mfaToken from POST /api/auth/login plus a TOTP code.

GET /api/api-keys/permissions.summary: Every scope a key may be issued with
GET /api/api-keys/permissions.description: The permission catalogue, so a client can build a key without hard-coding scope names, plus the purposes a key can be labelled with (rmm, siem, flexpoint, quickbooks, monitoring, scheduler, other).

GET /api/api-keys.description: Names, prefixes, scopes, owner, last use and state — never the secret and never its hash. `?includeRevoked=true` keeps the history.

POST /api/api-keys.summary: Issue a key for a program
POST /api/api-keys.description: The only time the secret is returned — store it in the client, and revoke the key if it is lost. The key acts as `userId` (the caller by default), intersected with `permissions`, so it can never exceed the account it borrows.

POST /api/api-keys/:id/rotate.summary: Issue a new secret for the same key
POST /api/api-keys/:id/rotate.description: Scopes, owner and name stay; the previous secret stops working immediately.

DELETE /api/api-keys/:id.description: Recorded as a state rather than a deletion, so the inventory keeps its history. Requests using the key are refused from the next call.

POST /api/events.summary: Receive an event from another system (RMM, SIEM, monitoring)
POST /api/events.description: The gateway every outside system sends to. Idempotent by (source, externalId): a repeat attaches to the ticket the first event opened and counts the occurrence, and `kind: recovery` closes that ticket instead of opening one. Needs ticket:create. Returns what happened — whether a ticket was opened, joined or closed — rather than only that the request was understood.

GET /api/events.summary: Recently received events, with the ticket each became
GET /api/events.description: Filter with ?source= and ?state=open|recovered. Useful for answering "did the RMM reach us?".

GET /api/events/sources.summary: Which systems have sent events, and how many

POST /api/flexpoint/sync.description: Reads customers, invoices and deposits according to the connection's options, stores them, links customers to clients, and records settled payments when that option is on. The same work the Sync button on C7NC → FlexPoint does. A scheduler can call this on a timer: FlexPoint publishes no webhooks, so nothing arrives on its own.

GET /api/flexpoint.summary: The FlexPoint picture: connection, options, counts, client receivables
GET /api/flexpoint.description: Everything the configuration page is drawn from, and the cheapest way to read a client's receivable in bulk.

PUT /api/flexpoint/options.description: What to pull, how customers are matched to clients, whether clients are created for unmatched customers, whether the client id is written back, whether settled payments are recorded, and whether invoices may be pushed. Writes to FlexPoint or to the ledger are off until switched on.

POST /api/flexpoint/link.summary: Tie a FlexPoint customer to a client, or untie it
POST /api/flexpoint/link.description: One customer per client — linking replaces any previous one. `customerId: null` clears the link without touching FlexPoint.

GET /api/flexpoint/clients/:companyId.description: Open balance, overdue, what has been received, the invoices FlexPoint holds, and the FlexPoint payments recorded here.

POST /api/flexpoint/invoices/:invoiceId/.summary: Create or update this invoice in FlexPoint
POST /api/flexpoint/invoices/:invoiceId/.description: Refused unless "push invoices" is switched on for the connection. Idempotent: an invoice that already carries a FlexPoint id is updated rather than created twice.

GET /api/flexpoint/invoices.summary: Local invoices with their FlexPoint state

POST /api/cloudconnect.description: kind, name, credentials and settings. `GET /api/cloudconnect/types` publishes what each connector needs, including the field labels and explanations the configuration dialog shows.

GET /api/cloudconnect/types.description: Every connector kind, what it does, the credentials it needs (with labels, hints and the vendor's own API reference) and the settings it honours.

POST /api/cloudconnect/:id/test.description: A real call to the provider. On failure the answer names the fields at fault and how to fix them.

POST /api/cloudconnect/:id/sync.description: For FlexPoint this runs the full FlexPoint sync (linking and payments included); for every other kind it stores what the adapter returned.

GET /api/cloudconnect/:id/synced-entitie.summary: What a connector has brought in

GET /api/cloudconnect/status.description: State, detail, when it was last verified and whether it is stale, without calling the provider.

POST /api/tickets.description: The same ticket a person would open, with the fields an integrator needs: board, client, contact, priority, assignee. Prefer POST /api/events for monitoring traffic — it is idempotent, and this is not.

requestExample.title: Printer offline
requestExample.description: Reported by the client's office manager.

GET /api/tickets.description: Filtered and paginated. A client-scoped credential only ever sees its own client's tickets.

PATCH /api/tickets/:id.description: Status, priority, assignment, board and the rest. Status changes are what fire the ticket's notifications.

POST /api/tickets/:id/comments.summary: Add a note or reply to a ticket
POST /api/tickets/:id/comments.description: `isInternal: true` keeps the note off the customer's copy, which is what an integration's working notes should be.

GET /api/clients.description: The client list, filterable by status, type, territory and search.

POST /api/clients.description: Only `name` is required. This is what the FlexPoint option "create clients for unmatched customers" calls internally.

POST /api/billing/invoices/generate.summary: Generate an invoice from unbilled time

POST /api/billing/invoices/:id/send.summary: Send an invoice to the client

POST /api/billing/invoices/:id/record-pa.summary: Record a payment against an invoice

POST /api/billing/batches/:id/approve.description: Issues every draft in the batch and offers each invoice to the connected accounting system. When the connection is FlexPoint and pushing is allowed, that push goes through FlexPoint's merchant API.

GET /api/service-alerts.description: What the alert banner and the Outage Board read.

GET /api/alert-webhooks.description: Where this application sends service_alert.raised and service_alert.resolved, with the signing secret and which events each endpoint wants.

POST /api/alert-webhooks/:id/test.summary: Send a test delivery to a webhook

GET /api/alert-webhooks/deliveries.summary: What was delivered, and what failed

GET /api/system/changelog.summary: What's New — the release notes as structured data

GET /api/system/audit-logs.description: Actions with their actor, entity and timestamp. This is the join an SIEM wants: correlate a detection with the change someone made after it.

GET /api/configuration.description: Every setting the application reads: value, source (default, environment, or saved), what changing it affects, and what it defaults to.

GET /api/portal/tickets.summary: The customer portal's own ticket list
GET /api/portal/tickets.description: Portal routes are authenticated by a contact's one-time code, not by a staff session — they are listed here so the surface is complete, not as something an integration should call.

GET /api/kb.description: The published articles, with /api/kb/drafts for the ones not published and /api/kb/categories for the tree.

GET /api/reports/:id/run.summary: Run a report and get its rows
GET /api/reports/:id/run.description: The custom report designer's runner: a stored template rendered against live data, returning the rows and the totals it computed.

GET /api/dashboard/layout.description: Per-user, not global: this is the arrangement of the widgets on the caller's own dashboard.
